# Tossie Buys Houses (Coastal GA Property Solutions, LLC)

> Cash home buyer serving Georgia, South Carolina, Florida, Alabama, North Carolina, and Tennessee.
> Buys residential property in any condition as a principal, with no commissions, fees, or repairs
> required from the seller. Written no-obligation offer in as little as 24 hours; closing typically
> 7 to 28 days. Founded and run by Tossie Griner of Savannah, Georgia.

- Buys occupied, tenant-occupied, vacant, fire damaged, and code-violation properties

## States and how the law differs
- [Georgia](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/sell-my-house-fast/georgia/): Non-judicial (power of sale) foreclosure. There is no right of redemption after a non-judicial foreclosure sale in Georgia. The 12-month redemption people hear about applies only to judicial foreclosures, which are rare here. Georgia real estate closings are conducted under the supervision of a licensed Georgia attorney, not a title agent working alone.
- [South Carolina](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/sell-my-house-fast/south-carolina/): Judicial foreclosure. There is no statutory right of redemption after the sale in South Carolina. What exists instead is the upset bid window: if the lender preserved its right to a deficiency judgment, bidding stays open until the 30th day after the sale. South Carolina requires a licensed South Carolina attorney to supervise the real estate closing.
- [Florida](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/sell-my-house-fast/florida/): Judicial foreclosure. Florida gives no post-sale statutory right of redemption. Your right to redeem ends when the certificate of sale is filed. Florida closings are normally handled by a title company or a closing agent; an attorney is not required.
- [Alabama](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/sell-my-house-fast/alabama/): Non-judicial (most common) foreclosure. Alabama is unusual in the Southeast: owners generally keep a one-year right of redemption after the foreclosure sale. That drops to 180 days when the loan originated on or after January 1, 2016, a homestead exemption was claimed for the tax year of the sale, and the lender gave the required redemption notice at least 30 days before the sale. Alabama closings are typically handled by a title company or closing attorney depending on the county's custom.
- [North Carolina](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/sell-my-house-fast/north-carolina/): Power of sale, court-authorized foreclosure. There is no post-sale redemption period. Instead, a 10-day upset bid window runs after the sale, and every new upset bid restarts a fresh 10-day clock. North Carolina requires an attorney to handle the title work and closing.
- [Tennessee](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/sell-my-house-fast/tennessee/): Non-judicial (trustee sale) foreclosure. Tennessee law provides a two-year right of redemption after the sale, but only if that right was not waived in the original deed of trust. In practice, most Tennessee deeds of trust waive it, so most owners have no redemption at all. Tennessee closings are usually handled by a title company or a closing attorney.

## Guides
- [The Georgia Foreclosure Timeline: How Little Time You Actually Have](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/guides/georgia-foreclosure-timeline/): Georgia foreclosures are non-judicial and can finish in about 60 days. There's no redemption after the sale. Here's the real timeline and where your exits are.
- [Florida Foreclosure Timeline: Why You Have Longer Than You Think, and Less Than You Need](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/guides/florida-foreclosure-timeline/): Florida foreclosure is judicial and typically takes 8 months to 2 years. But there's no redemption after the sale. Here's the sequence and where the exits are.
- [Alabama's Right of Redemption: One Year, or 180 Days, and Why It Rarely Helps](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/guides/alabama-right-of-redemption/): Alabama is one of the few states giving homeowners a redemption right after the foreclosure sale. Here's how it works, when it shrinks to 180 days, and its practical limits.
- [North Carolina's 10-Day Upset Bid: Why a Foreclosure Sale Isn't Final on Sale Day](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/guides/north-carolina-upset-bid/): NC foreclosures need a clerk's hearing first, and after the sale a 10-day upset bid window runs — restarting with every new bid. Here's what that means for you.
- [Tennessee Trustee Sales: Fast, and That Two-Year Redemption Probably Doesn't Apply to You](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/guides/tennessee-trustee-sale/): Tennessee foreclosures are non-judicial trustee sales. The two-year redemption right you'll read about is waived in most deeds of trust. Here's what's actually true.
- [South Carolina Foreclosure: The Master-in-Equity, the 30-Day Upset Bid, and No Redemption](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/guides/south-carolina-foreclosure-upset-bid/): SC foreclosures go through court, usually before a Master-in-Equity. There's no redemption after the sale — only a 30-day upset bid window, and only sometimes.
- [What Cash Home Buyers Actually Pay, and How the Offer Gets Built](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/guides/what-cash-buyers-actually-pay/): The real arithmetic behind a cash offer: after-repair value minus repairs, minus holding and closing costs, minus margin. Including where the '70% rule' comes from.
- [Selling an Inherited House: What Probate Actually Requires Before You Can Sell](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/guides/selling-inherited-house-probate/): You can't sell an inherited house until someone has legal authority to sign the deed. Here's how probate grants it, what it costs to wait, and what heirs can do meanwhile.
- [Cash Buyer vs. Listing With an Agent vs. iBuyer: The Honest Comparison](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/guides/cash-offer-vs-listing-vs-ibuyer/): Three ways to sell, three different tradeoffs. What each actually nets you, how long each takes, and which situations each one genuinely fits.
- [Selling a House With Liens: What Gets Paid, What Gets Negotiated, What Stops a Sale](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/guides/selling-house-with-liens/): Mortgages, judgments, tax liens, HOA balances, mechanic's liens. Which ones come off at closing, which need negotiating, and which actually block a transfer.
- [Selling a Rental Property With Tenants Still in It](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/guides/selling-rental-with-tenants/): Leases survive a sale. Here's what transfers, what notice you owe, what happens to the security deposit, and why you don't need to evict before selling.
- [What Selling a House 'As-Is' Actually Means (and What It Doesn't)](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/guides/sell-house-as-is-meaning/): As-is means you make no repairs. It does not mean you can hide known defects. Here's the difference, and what disclosure still applies in the Southeast.
- [Property Tax Sales in the Southeast: How Long You Really Have](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/guides/property-tax-sales-explained/): Delinquent property taxes lead to a tax sale, and the rules differ sharply by state. Redemption periods, what you can still do, and how they differ from foreclosure.
- [Selling the House During a Divorce Without Making It Worse](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/guides/selling-house-during-divorce/): Who has to sign, how proceeds get split, what a court order changes, and why a cash sale often ends the fight faster than a listing does.
- [The Vacant House Problem: Why Your Insurance May Already Have Lapsed](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/guides/vacant-house-insurance-problem/): Most homeowners policies restrict coverage after 30 to 60 days of vacancy. If you own an empty house, this is the most expensive thing you don't know.
- [How to Tell a Real Cash Buyer From a Wholesaler Shopping Your Contract](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/guides/avoid-cash-buyer-scams/): Four questions that separate an actual buyer from someone assigning your contract to a stranger — plus the contract clauses worth reading before you sign.
- [Closing Costs in the Southeast: Who Pays What, and What a Cash Sale Removes](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/guides/closing-costs-who-pays/): Attorney states, title states, transfer taxes, prorations. What a seller normally pays across GA, SC, FL, AL, NC and TN — and which of those a cash sale eliminates.
- [Do You Need a Realtor to Sell Your House? An Honest Answer](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/guides/do-i-need-a-realtor/): No, you don't legally need one. Here's when an agent clearly earns their commission, when they clearly don't, and how to tell which situation you're in.
- [Selling a Fire Damaged House: Insurance, Smoke, and Why Financing Disappears](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/guides/sell-house-fire-damage/): Fire damage isn't just what burned. Smoke, water, and mold follow it, financed buyers vanish, and the insurance decision shapes everything.
- [How Fast Can You Actually Sell a House? Every Option, Timed](https://tossiebuyshouses.com/guides/how-fast-can-you-sell-a-house/): Seven days to seven months, depending on how you sell. Here's what actually sets the floor on each option, and what you can and can't compress.

## Disclosure
Tossie Buys Houses buys property for its own account and does not act as the seller's real estate agent
or broker in these transactions. Legal summaries on the site are general information about state
law, sourced on each page, and are not legal advice.
